READABILITY.evidence: Names are mostly clear (durabilityManager, registerJob, onBatchDurable), but the struct isn't gofmt-aligned (`metricsDurableCommitDuration time.Duration` is misaligned). Public methods have one-line docs only. The tricky goroutine/WaitGroup relay in prepare() has no comments.

MAINTAINABILITY.evidence: WaitForDurabilityContext and WaitForJobDurabilityContext repeat the same ~80-line lock/ctx/close loop. commitEnv takes `db *DB` (tight coupling). Configuration is detected with a hack: `reflect.ValueOf(...BatchDurable).Pointer() != ...defaultBatchDurable`. Tracker fields are reached directly from db.go Metrics().

ROBUSTNESS.evidence: A NoSyncWait prepare error fires onBatchDurable twice (once from the goroutine, once from the error path in Commit). firstErr latches permanently, so after one failure every later wait fails. close() overwrites firstErr. The hidden expired-vs-unknown job test fails. Limits are named constants and locking is consistent.

C6-03-CASE1.evidence: The API changes are additive, but prepare() now spawns a goroutine per sync commit on every DB (`go func(){ b.walSyncWG.Wait() ... }()`), even when BatchDurable is unset. The NoSyncWait fsyncWait path is relayed through that goroutine and also fires BatchDurable. When BatchDurable is configured, newJobID adds DB-mutex work to every sync commit.
